title: Paul and Barnabas at Iconium, Lystra, Derbe, Return to Antioch

questions.question: At Iconium, Paul and Barnabas spoke boldly in the synagogue and a great number of both Jews and Greeks believed. But unbelieving Jews stirred up Gentiles and "poisoned their minds against..."?
options: the brothers
the apostles
the way of God
the teachings of Paul
questions.explanation: Acts 14:2 (ESV): "But the unbelieving Jews stirred up the Gentiles and poisoned their minds against the brothers."

questions.question: Despite opposition at Iconium, they remained there a long time. God bore witness to the word of his grace by granting what?
options: Signs and wonders to be done by their hands
Great boldness in speaking to the crowds
Dreams and visions to the people of the city
A spirit of peace in the midst of the opposition
questions.correctAnswer: Signs and wonders to be done by their hands
questions.explanation: Acts 14:3 (ESV): "So they remained for a long time, speaking boldly for the Lord, who bore witness to the word of his grace, granting signs and wonders to be done by their hands."

questions.question: At Lystra, Paul healed a man who had been crippled from birth and had never walked. What did the crowds conclude about Paul and Barnabas?
options: That the gods had come down to them in the likeness of men, calling Barnabas Zeus and Paul Hermes
That they were great prophets of the Jewish God
That they were divine healers sent from the heavens
That they were Caesar's special envoys with divine power
questions.correctAnswer: That the gods had come down to them in the likeness of men, calling Barnabas Zeus and Paul Hermes
questions.explanation: Acts 14:11-12 (ESV): "And when the crowds saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voices, saying in Lycaonian, 'The gods have come down to us in the likeness of men!' Barnabas they called Zeus, and Paul, Hermes..."

questions.question: The priest of Zeus brought oxen and garlands to make sacrifices to Paul and Barnabas. How did Paul and Barnabas respond?
options: They tore their garments, ran into the crowd, and urged the people to turn from these vain things to the living God
They fled to the countryside to avoid the pagan celebrations
They rebuked the priest firmly and commanded him to leave
They preached a sermon proving they were mortal men
questions.correctAnswer: They tore their garments, ran into the crowd, and urged the people to turn from these vain things to the living God
questions.explanation: Acts 14:14-15 (ESV): "But when the apostles Barnabas and Paul heard of it, they tore their garments and rushed out into the crowd, crying out, 'Men, why are you doing these things? We also are men, of like nature with you, and we bring you good news, that you should turn from these vain things to a living God...'"

questions.question: Jews came from Antioch and Iconium to Lystra. They won over the crowds and stoned Paul and dragged him out of the city, supposing him to be dead. What happened?
options: When the disciples gathered around him, he rose up and entered the city again
The Lord healed him of his wounds over three days
He was carried to a safe house and recovered slowly
He lay unconscious for two days before reviving
questions.correctAnswer: When the disciples gathered around him, he rose up and entered the city again
questions.explanation: Acts 14:20 (ESV): "But when the disciples gathered about him, he rose up and entered the city, and on the next day he went on with Barnabas to Derbe."

questions.question: After making many disciples in Derbe, Paul and Barnabas retraced their steps back through Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch. What did they do in each church?
options: Strengthened the souls of the disciples, encouraging them to continue in the faith, and appointed elders
Celebrated the Lord's Supper, baptized new believers, and read letters from Jerusalem
Collected offerings for the Jerusalem church from each congregation
Preached to the Jewish synagogues first before meeting with believers
questions.correctAnswer: Strengthened the souls of the disciples, encouraging them to continue in the faith, and appointed elders
questions.explanation: Acts 14:21-23 (ESV): "...they returned to Lystra and to Iconium and to Antioch, strengthening the souls of the disciples, encouraging them to continue in the faith... And when they had appointed elders for them in every church..."

questions.question: Paul and Barnabas told the disciples "through many tribulations we must enter..."?
options: the kingdom of God
eternal rest
the joy of our Lord
the new creation
questions.explanation: Acts 14:22 (ESV): "...saying that through many tribulations we must enter the kingdom of God."

questions.question: When Paul and Barnabas appointed elders, they committed the congregations to whom?
options: The Lord in whom they had believed
The apostles in Jerusalem
The elders they had appointed
The Holy Spirit who would guide them
questions.correctAnswer: The Lord in whom they had believed
questions.explanation: Acts 14:23 (ESV): "And when they had appointed elders for them in every church, with prayer and fasting they committed them to the Lord in whom they had believed."

questions.question: When Paul and Barnabas returned to Antioch, they gathered the church and reported what?
options: All that God had done with them, and how he had opened a door of faith to the Gentiles
The number of churches founded and converts baptized
The opposition they faced and how God had delivered them
Their plans for a second missionary journey to new territories
questions.correctAnswer: All that God had done with them, and how he had opened a door of faith to the Gentiles
questions.explanation: Acts 14:27 (ESV): "And when they arrived and gathered the church together, they declared all that God had done with them, and how he had opened a door of faith to the Gentiles."

questions.question: In his speech about turning from idols to the living God, Paul said God "did not leave himself without witness." What witnesses did God leave?
options: He did good by giving you rains from heaven and fruitful seasons, satisfying your hearts with food and gladness
He preserved your life generation after generation in great mercy
He wrote his law in every human heart from the beginning
He created the heavens and earth and all men know this
questions.correctAnswer: He did good by giving you rains from heaven and fruitful seasons, satisfying your hearts with food and gladness
questions.explanation: Acts 14:17 (ESV): "Yet he did not leave himself without witness, for he did good by giving you rains from heaven and fruitful seasons, satisfying your hearts with food and gladness."

questions.question: After their return to Antioch from the first missionary journey, how long did they stay there?
options: No small time
About six months
A full year
Several weeks
questions.explanation: Acts 14:28 (ESV): "And they remained no little time with the disciples."

questions.question: Paul described God as "the living God, who made the heaven and the earth and the sea and all that is in them." In past generations God had allowed all the nations to do what?
options: Walk in their own ways
Follow their own gods
Live without revelation
Seek him independently
questions.explanation: Acts 14:16 (ESV): "In past generations he allowed all the nations to walk in their own ways."

questions.question: Why did the crowd at Lystra call Barnabas Zeus and Paul Hermes specifically?
options: Because Paul was the chief speaker
Because Barnabas was the taller and older man
Because the oracle at the temple had prophesied it
Because Paul was dressed in the style of Hermes worshippers
questions.correctAnswer: Because Paul was the chief speaker
questions.explanation: Acts 14:12 (ESV): "Barnabas they called Zeus, and Paul, Hermes, because he was the chief speaker."

questions.question: The crippled man at Lystra heard Paul speaking. Paul looked at him intently and saw what in him?
options: Faith to be made well
Openness to receive the word
Readiness to believe in Christ
Hunger for the healing power
questions.explanation: Acts 14:9 (ESV): "He listened to Paul speaking. And Paul, looking intently at him and seeing that he had faith to be made well,"

questions.question: The city of Lystra is said to be in the region of which area of modern Turkey?
options: Lycaonia
Pamphylia
Galatia proper
Pisidia
questions.explanation: Acts 14:6,11 (ESV) mentions Lycaonia in connection with Lystra and Derbe, and the crowd spoke in the Lycaonian language.

key_verse_text: "...saying that through many tribulations we must enter the kingdom of God."
